_about: Unit costs for the budget-constrained allocator (pipeline/15_optimize.py, issue #67). Every entry must carry a real source. Entries with sourced=false are refused by the optimizer rather than guessed at: the budget optimizer was cut from the original build precisely because inventing costs would have produced authoritative-looking allocations resting on nothing.
_price_year_note: Costs are NOT inflation-adjusted. The allocator compares interventions against each other, so a common price year matters more than currency-of-the-day, but absolute rupee totals should be read as 2020 prices.

cool_roof_lime.label: Cool roof, white lime paint
cool_roof_lime._derivation: NRDC reports the Ahmedabad Cool Roofs Pilot Program used simple white lime paint at approximately Rs 0.5 per square foot, reapplied every 4-5 years. Converted at 10.7639 sq ft per m2: 0.5 x 10.7639 = Rs 5.38/m2.
cool_roof_lime.source: NRDC, 'Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Cool Roofs', 2020-05-27, question 11 and Table 1.
cool_roof_lime.notes: The most defensible figure available here, because it is what an Indian municipality actually paid in a real city-scale programme rather than a retail quote. Cheapest option and the shortest-lived.

cool_roof_coating.label: Cool roof, reflective coating
cool_roof_coating._derivation: NRDC Table 1 gives coatings at Rs 20-40 per sq ft. Converted at 10.7639 sq ft per m2: Rs 215.3-430.6/m2, midpoint Rs 322.9.
cool_roof_coating.source: NRDC, 'Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Cool Roofs', 2020-05-27, Table 1: Indicative costs of cool roofs material types.
cool_roof_coating.notes: NRDC states a 1.5-2 year payback from cooling-energy savings, which this allocator does not model. Lifetime is indicative; the source gives payback, not lifespan.

cool_roof_tiles.label: Cool roof, tiles
cool_roof_tiles._derivation: NRDC Table 1 gives cool roof tiles at Rs 50-100 per sq ft, converted at 10.7639 sq ft per m2.
cool_roof_tiles.source: NRDC, 'Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Cool Roofs', 2020-05-27, Table 1.

native_trees.label: Native tree planting and green corridors
native_trees._why_unsourced: No credible Indian municipal or peer-reviewed unit cost was found. Searches returned commercial nursery and landscaping quotes (roughly Rs 50-800 per sapling) which vary by an order of magnitude, mix retail with programme costs, and exclude the multi-year establishment watering that dominates urban tree survival. Published Indian work reports benefit-cost RATIOS for urban greening (about 3:1 in npj Urban Sustainability 2025 for Lucknow, Chennai and Surat) but not the per-unit costs an allocator needs.
native_trees.what_would_close_this: A BMC or state horticulture schedule of rates, or a published urban-forestry programme cost including establishment maintenance.

pocket_parks.label: Pocket parks and green open space
pocket_parks._why_unsourced: Dominated by land acquisition, which in Mumbai varies by more than an order of magnitude between wards and swamps construction cost entirely. A single city-wide per-m2 figure would be meaningless.

cooling_centres.label: Cooling centres
cooling_centres._why_unsourced: Indian heat action plans describe cooling centres qualitatively; no capital or operating cost per centre was found. Cost also depends heavily on whether existing public buildings are retrofitted or new ones built.

rain_gardens.label: Rain gardens and water-sensitive urban design
rain_gardens._why_unsourced: No Indian unit cost found. Available figures are from US and Australian WSUD programmes with different labour costs and design standards.
